key_insight: A multimodal pretreatment biomarker model improved prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced NSCLC compared with PD-L1 or TMB alone, but performance was still only moderate.
clinical_relevance: This suggests that resistance risk assessment for advanced NSCLC may benefit from combining clinical, blood-based, and tumor-immune features rather than relying on a single biomarker.
method: Prospective multicentre study across 17 centers (PIONeeR), enrolling adults with advanced NSCLC starting anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.
Pretreatment profiling integrated six layers: clinical data, routine labs, circulating immune phenotyping, soluble vascular markers, digital pathology, transcriptomics, and genomics.
Compared 36 feature-selection methods and 10 machine-learning models using a .632 optimism-correction framework.
evidence_signal: In 435 evaluable patients, the multimodal signature reached an optimism-corrected AUROC of 0.73±0.05 and PPV of 0.63±0.07 overall, outperforming PD-L1 and TMB.
watch_item: The model’s value is promising but limited by only moderate discrimination and reduced PPV in first-line patients, so external validation and implementation testing are still needed.
paper_title: Multimodal profiling for prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer: the prospective PIONeeR biomarkers study
